title: Ancient Trees in the United States: Cities to Explore
meta_description: American cities register their trees with real precision. Five mapped cities, coast to coast, from Washington's 1912 cherries to Chicago's prairie oaks.
intro: American cities record their trees the way they record everything else, in public registers with dates attached, which makes the United States unusually good ground for this site's kind of verification. New York designates Great Trees, the National Park Service keeps witness trees with named histories, and Boston's Arnold Arboretum holds accession cards going back to the 1870s. Five cities are mapped so far, coast to coast: the two original 1912 cherry trees of Washington's Tidal Basin, an elm on a Manhattan corner that survived everything the twentieth century threw at it, Chicago's bur oaks that predate the city itself, and a Portland beech planted around the turn of the twentieth century. The oldest trees here are not Europe's yews, but the documentation is often better: core samples, planting ledgers, and champions measured to the centimetre.
